items.value: Four of the five countries (UK, Denmark, New Zealand, Australia) have more than four time zones; Brazil has exactly four
items.reasoning: Counted with overseas/dependent territories included: the United Kingdom spans about 9 zones (Pitcairn to the Indian Ocean territories), Australia about 9 (Cocos +6:30, Christmas +7, three mainland zones, Lord Howe, Norfolk, Macquarie), Denmark 5 (Denmark, Faroes and the several Greenland zones) and New Zealand 5 (NZST, Chatham +12:45, Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau). Brazil has exactly four (UTC-2 for Fernando de Noronha, -3, -4, -5), so it fails the 'more than four' test. That territories must be counted is confirmed by the options themselves: excluding them, every one of the five would be at four or fewer and the count would be zero, which no option offers.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — breakfast time in the two cities falls on different dates, but Anadyr is a day ahead of Nome, not behind
items.reasoning: Anadyr (Chukotka) keeps UTC+12 while Nome (Alaska) keeps UTC-9, a gap of 21 hours across the International Date Line, so when either city is at breakfast the other is on a different calendar date — statement I's substance holds. Statement II reverses the direction: Anadyr lies west of the Date Line and is therefore AHEAD, so when it is Monday in Anadyr it is generally still Sunday in Nome, not Tuesday. Note the stem's 'a few kilometers from each other' is loose — Anadyr and Nome are roughly 800 km apart; the few-kilometres illustration properly belongs to the Diomede Islands, which sit in the same two time zones.

items.value: 'Periyar' E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker founded the Self-Respect Movement
items.reasoning: The Self-Respect Movement (Suyamariyathai Iyakkam) was launched in the Madras Presidency in 1925 by E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker, 'Periyar', after he left the Congress, as a rationalist anti-caste and anti-Brahminical movement. Ambedkar led the Mahad and temple-entry satyagrahas and founded bodies such as the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha, not this movement; Bhaskarrao Jadhav and Dinkarrao Javalkar were non-Brahmin/Satyashodhak leaders in Maharashtra.

items.value: All three pairs are correct — Botswana/diamond, Chile/lithium, Indonesia/nickel
items.reasoning: Botswana is among the world's leading diamond producers, with the Orapa and Jwaneng mines and the Debswana joint venture dominating its economy. Chile holds part of the Lithium Triangle and is one of the top two lithium producers, extracting brine from the Salar de Atacama. Indonesia is the world's largest nickel producer and has used export restrictions on nickel ore to build domestic smelting capacity.

items.value: Both statements are correct and the phosphorescent property of rare earths is precisely why they are used in screens
items.reasoning: Rare earth compounds are used as the phosphors in flat display panels — europium for red, terbium for green, yttrium as the host lattice — so statement I is correct. Statement II is also correct: rare earth ions have sharp, efficient luminescent (phosphorescent) emission arising from their shielded 4f electronic transitions. The two are causally linked, not merely both true: it is that luminescent behaviour that makes them the material of choice for screens, so II explains I.

items.value: Statements I and II are the incorrect ones — the National Rail Plan targets 2030, and Kavach is indigenous, not German
items.reasoning: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. The National Rail Plan aims at a 'future ready' railway system by 2030 (with Vision 2024 for accelerated near-term works), not 2028, so I is incorrect. Kavach was developed indigenously by RDSO with Indian industry partners and is India's own Train Collision Avoidance System, not a German collaboration, so II is incorrect. Statement III is correct — Kavach relies on RFID tags fixed to the track in station sections, yards and block sections to give the locomotive its exact location — so III is excluded from the answer.

items.value: All three missions encourage and support micro-gravity research
items.reasoning: Axiom-4 carried a crew to the International Space Station with a dedicated slate of micro-gravity experiments, including ISRO-designed studies. Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme, whose crewed flights and follow-on Bharatiya Antariksh Station are explicitly meant to enable micro-gravity science. SpaDeX, besides demonstrating the docking technology on which a long-duration micro-gravity platform depends, flew alongside POEM-4, which hosted micro-gravity payloads such as the plant-growth CROPS experiment. The judgement call is SpaDeX, whose headline objective is docking; the stem's softer wording 'encourage and support' rather than 'conduct' is what brings it in.

items.value: Two pairs are correct — Dornier-228 as maritime patrol and C-17 as transport; the IL-76 is not a supersonic combat aircraft
items.reasoning: The Dornier Do-228, licence-built by HAL, is flown by the Indian Navy and Coast Guard for maritime surveillance and patrol, so pair I is right. The C-17 Globemaster III is the IAF's heavy-lift strategic transport, so pair III is right. The Ilyushin Il-76 is a subsonic heavy military transport (and the platform for the IAF's Phalcon AEW&C and the earlier flight-refuelling variants) — it is neither supersonic nor a combat aircraft, so pair II fails.

items.value: Cloud seeding uses silver iodide and potassium iodide
items.reasoning: Artificial rain-making seeds clouds with substances whose crystal structure mimics ice, giving water vapour a nucleus on which to condense and freeze. Silver iodide and potassium iodide are the standard glaciogenic seeding agents (dry ice and hygroscopic salts such as sodium chloride are the other common choices). Silver nitrate and potassium nitrate/chloride are not the reagents used for this purpose, which rules out B, C and D.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — the pardoning power is open to limited judicial review, but it is exercised on ministerial advice
items.reasoning: The Supreme Court has held in Maru Ram, Kehar Singh and most explicitly Epuru Sudhakar (2006) that although the merits of a pardon are not justiciable, the exercise of Article 72 power can be reviewed on limited grounds such as mala fides, arbitrariness, non-application of mind or reliance on wholly irrelevant material — so I is correct. Statement II is wrong: Article 72 power, like the President's other functions, is exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74, so the President cannot act independently of the Central Government.

items.value: Statements I and III are correct; there is no constitutional requirement that the Speaker resign from his or her party
items.reasoning: Statement I restates the proviso to Article 94: on dissolution the Speaker does not vacate office until immediately before the first sitting of the next House. Statement III restates Article 94(c) with its proviso — removal by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, on at least fourteen days' notice. Statement II is false: severing party ties on election as Speaker is a British convention, not an Indian constitutional command; the Tenth Schedule merely protects a Speaker who chooses to give up party membership, which presupposes that doing so is optional.

items.value: Neither statement is correct — anti-defection questions are decided by the Speaker, and the Constitution does mention political parties
items.reasoning: Under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule a question of disqualification on ground of defection is decided by the Chairman or the Speaker of the House concerned, and that decision is final; the President-on-the-Election-Commission's-opinion route of Article 103 is expressly confined to the other disqualifications and does not apply here — and in no case does the President act on the opinion of the Council of Ministers for this purpose. Statement II is also false: the Tenth Schedule, inserted by the Fifty-second Amendment in 1985, uses the expression 'political party' repeatedly in defining defection, merger and the Speaker's exemption.

items.value: Statement I is wrong — States do make the rules for minor mineral concessions — while Statement II is right, the Centre notifies minor minerals
items.reasoning: Section 15 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 expressly empowers State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases and other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals, so statement I is incorrect. Statement II is correct: Section 3(e) defines minor minerals and allows the Central Government to declare any other mineral to be a minor mineral by notification in the Official Gazette — which is how minerals have periodically been moved into that category. Since I is false and II is true, the explanatory options A and B and the option C do not arise.

items.value: The European Union enacted the Nature Restoration Law
items.reasoning: The Nature Restoration Regulation is EU legislation, proposed by the European Commission under the European Green Deal and Biodiversity Strategy and finally adopted by the Council in June 2024; it sets binding targets to restore degraded ecosystems across member States. The World Bank and the OECD are not law-making bodies for their members, and the FAO issues standards and guidelines rather than binding law, so none of them could 'enact' such a law.

items.value: All three statements are incorrect
items.reasoning: The question asks which statements are NOT correct, and all three fail. Article 243B(2) allows a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakhs to dispense with Panchayats at the intermediate level, so they do not exist in all States. Article 243F fixes the minimum age for membership of a Panchayat at twenty-one years, not thirty. And Article 243-I places the duty of constituting the State Finance Commission to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend the distribution of tax proceeds on the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — BIMSTEC had seven members as of January 2025; the rest of the statements fail
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct: BIMSTEC's membership stood at seven — Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Statement II is wrong: the grouping was born as BIST-EC with the Bangkok Declaration of 6 June 1997, not a Dhaka Declaration of 1999. Statement III is wrong because Nepal was not a founding member — the founders were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand, with Myanmar joining later in 1997 and Nepal and Bhutan only in 2004. Statement IV turns on the 2021-22 restructuring of the fourteen sectors into seven pillars, under which tourism became a sub-sector of People-to-People Contact, led by Nepal; India leads the Security pillar. Confidence is LOW because if the older fourteen-sector allocation (in which India led Tourism) is the intended benchmark, the answer would be C instead.

items.value: The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha are on the jury; the President is not
items.reasoning: The jury for the Gandhi Peace Prize is chaired by the Prime Minister of India and includes the Chief Justice of India, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the single largest opposition party), and two eminent persons. The President of India is not a member of the jury — the President's role is to confer the award at the presentation ceremony, which is the confusion the item is testing, so statements II, III and IV alone are right.

items.value: Statements I and II only — GAGAN's benefits are not confined to aviation
items.reasoning: GAGAN is India's satellite-based augmentation system, jointly developed by ISRO and the AAI, and its stated purpose is to add accuracy and integrity (including alerts when the signal cannot be trusted) to GPS positions over the Indian region, so I is correct. That integrity assurance is what permits GAGAN-based approach procedures and hence more uniform, higher-quality air traffic management, so II is correct. Statement III is wrong: GAGAN's signal is openly usable and has been applied well beyond aviation — in railways, maritime navigation, precision agriculture, surveying and disaster management.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — India co-chaired the Paris summit, but the US and the UK did not sign the declaration
items.reasoning: The AI Action Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris in February 2025 was co-chaired by France and India, and was explicitly framed as the successor to the Bletchley Park Summit of 2023 and the Seoul Summit of 2024, so statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong on its central claim: the United States and the United Kingdom conspicuously declined to sign the summit's Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet, even though around sixty other countries did — that refusal was the summit's most-reported outcome.

items.value: All four pairs are correctly matched
items.reasoning: The UN General Assembly designated 2025 the International Year of Peace and Trust, 2026 the International Year of the Woman Farmer, 2027 the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, and 2029 the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence — the last timed to the close approach of the asteroid Apophis in April 2029. Each of the four rows therefore matches its declared year, so no pair can be struck out.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct; the summit theme was 'multilateralism', not 'multiculturalism'
items.reasoning: The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan in October 2024 under Russia's chairship, so statement I is correct, and Indonesia was admitted as a full member of BRICS in January 2025, so statement II is correct. Statement III substitutes one word: the declared theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', and multilateralism — reform of global governance and de-dollarised settlement — rather than multiculturalism was the summit's subject, so III fails and options B and C fall with it.

items.value: Only statement III is correct — the minimum age for the Chairperson or a Member is forty-five years
items.reasoning: Statement III restates the eligibility bar in the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 that no person below forty-five years of age may assume office as Chairperson or Member. The other three fail: the Act's reach extends to public servants both in and outside India, so I is wrong; the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India, a former Judge of the Supreme Court or an eminent person meeting the prescribed criteria, so the word 'only' in II is wrong even though its first clause about Parliament and State legislatures is right; and the Act does permit inquiry into allegations against a sitting Prime Minister, subject to excluded subjects such as international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space and to approval by a full bench with at least a two-thirds majority, so IV is wrong.

items.value: Only statement I is correct — the tournament was in Delhi, but the two winning margins have been swapped between the men's and women's finals
items.reasoning: The inaugural Kho Kho World Cup was staged in New Delhi in January 2025, so statement I holds. The scores in II and III are interchanged: India's men beat Nepal 54-36 in the men's final, while India's women beat Nepal by the wider 78-40 margin in the women's final. Both India teams did win, which is what makes the item easy to over-credit, but as printed each of statements II and III attaches the other final's scoreline, so neither can be counted correct.

items.value: Only statement II is correct — Abhimanyu Mishra is the youngest ever Grandmaster; Gukesh's title came against Ding Liren at the World Championship, not at the Olympiad
items.reasoning: Statement I confuses two separate 2024 events and gets the opponent wrong as well. The 45th Chess Olympiad at Budapest is a team event, which India won in both the open and women's sections; Gukesh Dommaraju became the youngest ever World Chess Champion in December 2024 at Singapore by defeating Ding Liren of China, not Ian Nepomniachtchi of Russia. Statement II is correct: Abhimanyu Mishra of the United States earned the Grandmaster title in June 2021 aged 12 years and about 4 months, breaking Sergey Karjakin's long-standing record.
